name: 0/1 Knapsack
description: Classic DP problem: given items with weights and values, find maximum value achievable within a weight capacity. Each item can be taken at most once (0 or 1).
aim: Maximize total value of selected items without exceeding weight capacity, using a 2D DP table where dp[i][w] = max value using first i items with capacity w.
howItWorks: For each item i and capacity w:
If weight[i] > w: dp[i][w] = dp[i-1][w] (skip item)
Trace back through table to find which items were selected

time.averageCase: Pseudo-polynomial — linear in n and W

complexity.spaceDescription: 2D table of size (n+1)×(W+1); can optimize to O(W) with 1D array

realWorld: Resource allocation — maximize ROI within budget
Portfolio optimization — select investments within capital limit
Cargo loading — maximize value within weight limit
whenToUse: Capacity is reasonably bounded (not too large)
Each item chosen at most once
alternatives: Fractional Knapsack — O(n log n) greedy if items are divisible
Greedy won't work here — counterexamples exist
Branch and Bound — for larger instances with pruning

inputHint: The FIRST number is the capacity, then pairs of (weight, value).
